## Highlights

- A [custom provider](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#define-a-custom-provider) in front of an LLM gateway, such as Bifrost or LiteLLM, works like a shipped provider ([#5064](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5064)):
  - A base URL that is not the API root says so. When the address answers with a web page or has no model list (a gateway's dashboard address without `/v1`, say), the credential row, **Check models** and **Refresh catalogs** read "The base URL answered with a web page, not a model list. Check that it is the API root; for most gateways it ends in /v1." in English, German or French, instead of a JSON parser's message, and Tale asks the address once instead of three times.
  - Models a gateway lists without saying what they support carry what Tale knows about them. Behind a Bifrost gateway, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT 5.6 Luna and GPT 5.6 Sol now see the pictures attached in chat, take tools and offer an effort setting; before, all three read as taking none of these, so **Auto** passed them over and an attached picture reached them only as a mention. A model Tale does not know is offered with tools and without image input, and an embedding, speech or image model that Tale recognizes is no longer offered in chat.
  - A chat gets its title when its model thinks first or would answer the message instead: the namer receives the first message as text to name, and a model that spends the title's budget thinking gets room and time for it. Claude behind a gateway named its chats in one call, where the chats used to keep the title made from their first words.
  - The model menu reads a version Anthropic spells with dashes the way it is said, "Claude Sonnet 5.5" rather than "Claude Sonnet 5 5", and its search matches a model's ID: `gpt-5.6` finds GPT 5.6 Luna.
- The Anthropic provider offers Claude Sonnet 5.5, with its 1M-token context window, image input, tools and effort setting, at USD 2 per million input and USD 10 per million output tokens ([#5064](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5064)).
- [Video ingestion](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/video-ingestion) fetches YouTube videos without captions again, and gets past proxies that a platform turns away ([#5066](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5066)):
  - The image brings yt-dlp 2026.10.26. YouTube refused the audio downloads of the earlier version from every network, so every video without captions failed at its audio step.
  - Through [`OUTBOUND_PROXY_URLS`](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/video-ingestion#egress-proxy), a video keeps one proxy for its metadata, captions and audio, starting on the proxy through which its platform last served a video. When the platform turns it away there with a bot check, a rate limit or a refused request, or the proxy fails, it moves to the next proxy that has not failed it, with up to five attempts per step and none started after 90 seconds. Before, every step took the next proxy in turn, and the first refusal failed the video. Through 100 shared data-center proxies, about two thirds of which YouTube turned away, 5 of 5 test videos came through with their metadata, captions and audio.
- [Image models that cannot use tools](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#choose-a-model-when-the-choice-matters) are no longer offered as chat models. Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, GPT-5 Image and the Lyria music models failed every message there, because every reply can call tools such as a document search. To get a picture, ask for one in the conversation: the assistant creates it with the organization's image model ([#5062](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5062)).

## Upgrade notes

- No migration runs, and the API contract stays at `3.49.0`.
- In an organization with a custom provider whose model listing does not describe its models (an LLM gateway, or a server's bare `/v1/models`), those models now count as taking tools, and the ones Tale's catalogs know also as reading images and taking an effort setting. **Auto** can now choose them where it passed them over, pictures attached in chat are sent to them as images, which the vendor bills as image input, and the model endpoints for API keys no longer refuse their tools or images. An embedding, speech or image model that such a listing names, and that Tale's catalogs know as one, leaves the chat model lists.
- **Auto** no longer chooses a model that charges nothing for its output, such as OpenRouter's ScaleDown text compressors, which its price fallback used to prefer.
- A chat title from a model known to think, or from one that spent the title's 48 tokens thinking, may now use up to 2,048 output tokens and 30 seconds, booked like any other title.
- For video ingestion through `OUTBOUND_PROXY_URLS`, list a proxy provider's fixed-address endpoints, often numbered user names on one gateway, instead of one rotating endpoint. YouTube can refuse a download from another address than the one that asked for it, and a rotating endpoint gives every connection a new address. `VIDEO_INGEST_PROXY_URL` can instead give video a proxy of its own, which, as a single proxy, does not repeat a refused attempt. The worker logs each move by the proxy's position in the list, never its credentials. Recreate the backend and `sandbox-egress` after changing the list. A yt-dlp of your own (`VIDEO_INGEST_BIN_DIR`) older than 2026.10.26 makes the worker warn; upgrade it.
- A chat or an agent on an image model that takes no tools is now refused, and a saved chat model pick on one falls back to **Auto**. `GET /api/v1/models` and the model endpoints for API keys no longer list such models. OpenRouter text models without tool support, such as Phi 4, Sonar, o1-pro and Gemma, are still listed and fail the same way ([#5063](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5063)).
